title: Dynamic Opportunity Scorer for multi-cycle roadmap allocation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current RICE-derived scoring sheets are static per-cycle and do not capture cross-cycle diminishing returns, stochastic demand, or token-cost elasticity. As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private workloads, product decisions need to account for multi-cycle resource allocation: when to spend limited engineering cycles on latency-sensitive runtime improvements vs. long-term cost-savings (quantization, caching) that compound over time.

Goal: Design and validate the Dynamic Opportunity Scorer (DOS) — a prioritization layer that extends RICE with: scenario-weighted value (traffic/vertical), multi-cycle impact profiles, token-cost elasticity, and latency-regret curves. DOS outputs an allocation recommendation (points or committed FTE%) per initiative across a planning horizon (N cycles) and maps to OKR contributions.

Approach:
1) Formalize value streams: map initiatives to OKRs and estimate immediate value (reach * impact) and recurring value (monthly net savings or revenue uplift).
2) Extend RICE inputs: add "recurrence" multiplier, elasticity factor (sensitivity of unit economics to token/latency improvements), and scenario weights (best/expected/worst traffic).
3) Run Monte Carlo simulations across N=6 cycles sampling traffic growth, adoption lags, and rollout slippage to produce a distribution of cumulative value and cost for each candidate.
4) Introduce a cycle-aware diminishing-returns function so consecutive investments in similar verticals show decreasing marginal return unless paired with enabling work (e.g., runtime kernel improvements).
5) Produce a ranked allocation plan with recommended start cycle, phased investment (X points in cycle 1, Y in cycle 2...), and confidence bands.

Deliverables: DOS scoring spreadsheet + simulation notebook, a lightweight UI wireframe for Console to show per-initiative multi-cycle allocation, and a one-pager playbook for PMs mapping DOS outputs to Linear tickets and OKR updates.
acceptance_criteria: DOS scoring spreadsheet accepts initiatives with fields: reach, impact, confidence, recurrence, elasticity, estimated engineering points, dependencies
Monte Carlo simulation runs (N=10k) and produces distribution of cumulative value and ROI for each initiative across 6 cycles
Output CSV contains recommended per-cycle point allocation and start cycle for top 12 initiatives
Playbook documents how to convert DOS recommendations into Linear tickets and OKR targets
Prototype Console wireframe showing per-initiative cumulative value curve and uncertainty bands reviewed by design and engineering
success_metrics: Framework adoption: 80% of roadmap features in Cycle 2026-W02 are scored with DOS inputs
Decision confidence: average uncertainty (stddev of ROI) reduced by 30% vs. static RICE across sampled initiatives
Economic impact: roadmap allocation using DOS yields >=5% projected token-cost savings or >=7% latency improvement for latency-sensitive OKRs over 4 cycles in simulation
Operationalization: 90% of recommendations converted into Linear tickets with planned start cycle
tradeoffs: Increased inputs per initiative will raise PM overhead — mitigated by templates and default priors
Monte Carlo adds computation and may slow cadence; start with offline runs and move to cached nightly simulations
More conservative allocations may under-invest in optional, high-reward bets — provide adjustable risk appetite knob
risks: Model risk: bad priors (elasticity/recurrence) could bias allocations — require calibrated priors and historical backtesting
Stakeholder buy-in: engineering may resist phased multi-cycle allocations without clearer rollout commitments
Data quality: insufficient traffic/usage segmentation will produce noisy scenario weights
